title: Reserve Bank Amendment (Australian Reconstruction and Development Board) Bill 2013

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would create an Australian Reconstruction and Development Board within the Reserve Bank to restructure financial arrangements and provide finance for at-risk agricultural industries.
It would give the board responsibility for rural reconstruction and development policy, including research, tailored funding and use of the bank’s capital to implement policy.
The main amendments would begin on the 28th day after Royal Assent, and the Reserve Bank Board’s policy would take priority where their policies conflicted.
changes: The bank would gain an express power to acquire, hold and dispose of property.
The board would include the Governor, a bank representative and seven members with rural or agricultural experience.
The board would report annually to the Treasurer on its actions, their effects and policy changes.
summary.affected: Agricultural enterprises, associated industries and infrastructure, sectors identified as needing reconstruction or development, and the Reserve Bank are affected.

speeches.speaker: Bob Katter
speeches.brief: Presented a bill proposing a revolving fund of $420 million and borrowing powers for an Australian Reconstruction and Development Board to support agriculture. Argued that rural industries faced severe debt pressures, citing declining farm equity, rising debt and threatened forced sales, and sought a mechanism to sustain producers until stronger markets, including ethanol demand from China, emerged.
